independent_review.scope: read-only independent review of IntegerSieve constructor; no live source mutation
independent_review.conclusion: No correctness, capacity, ordering, or ownership blocker for valid maxn >= 0.
proofs: table_size(maxn)>=1 for valid input, so lpf[0], limit-1 are defined. 0 and 1 remain zero after sentinel initialization.
Even entries remain 2. On odd indices, sentinel 2 cannot equal a valid smallest prime factor, which is >=3.
Every odd composite x is generated from i=x/p with its least prime p and p<=lpf(i). Since p>=3, i<=N/3, so excluding propagation for i>N/3 cannot remove a required write.
The inclusive cutoff (limit-1)/3 includes exactly all possible i with 3*i<=maxn. Tail iterates the next odd index without gaps or duplicates.
The unchanged ascending i sequence and push order preserve an increasing prime_list; prime2 is inserted first exactly for maxn>=2.

The existing table_size capacity guard is preserved. For supported 32-bit int GCC/Clang, all uint64_t products are at most INT_MAX squared; size_t increments stay below representable allocated bounds.
All storage remains vector-owned. If lpf allocation or prime-list growth throws, constructor unwinding frees all already-constructed vectors; no externally visible object is published.
independent_review.contract_note: SKIP_RUNTIME_CHECKS with negative maxn is outside the API precondition. In particular maxn=-1 may produce a zero-length vector before lpf[0]; no claim is made that invalid input remains safe under skip.
independent_review.existing_validation_reviewed: tail_test.log: GCC/Clang checked/skip and Clang ASan+UBSan checked/skip, each independent reference, exception, full initialization PASS. No mechanically redundant re-run added.
independent_review.performance_note: Preserve parent measured small-process wall-time regression separately from Sieve API timing. A 7.5% increase from about 0.83 to 0.89ms is not described as API improvement.
